newsitem.title: USA: Campbell, Heinz in mediation on executive.
newsitem.headline: Campbell, Heinz in mediation on executive.

text.p: Mediation was to begin Monday between Campbell Soup Co and H.J. Heinz Co in a dispute over Heinz's hiring of a top Campbell executive, the companies said.
Campbell spokesman Kevin Lowery said Campbell had agreed to the mediation providing the executive, Daniel O'Neill, did not work for Heinz for the duration of the mediation.
A Campbell lawsuit against Heinz continues, Lowery said.
"We have agreed to mediation, but we only agreed to it on the stipulation that (O'Neill) would not work there," Lowery said.
Campbell contends that O'Neill, the former head of Campbell's U.S. soup division, is bound by a non-compete agreement and cannot work for Heinz.
Heinz, which hired O'Neill to head its pet food and Star-Kist tuna operations, and O'Neill had sued Campbell in Pennsylvania state court to release him from the agreement.
Campbell in turn sued in U.S. District Court in Camden, N.J., to block O'Neill from working for Heinz.
A hearing on Campbell's suit has been scheduled for February 3, Lowery said.
Heinz spokeswoman Debbie Foster said she could not confirm O'Neill's employment status during the mediation process.
"He is working with a mediator this week. I can't tell you technically whether that means he is or is not working for Heinz. He has been here and he was working for Heinz last week," Foster said.
Heinz said Friday that O'Neill's job at the company did not put him in a position to compete with Campbell and that O'Neill and Heinz had signed an agreement protecting Campbell's business secrets.
